paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin that routes model traffic through any new-api-family relay panel (one-
api / new-api / Veloera / done-hub / ...)
English | 中文
## Features
- **Panels** — the *Connection* tab is an **accordion**: every connected panel is a collapsible row
(account, balance, synced models, active key at a glance — the account line fills in lazily, so one
unreachable panel never blocks the list), and expanding it folds the panel's four sub-tabs (API keys
/ models / dashboard / usage logs) inline; at most one panel is expanded at a time. New panels are
added with *Add panel*: name (immutable after creation — it names the dsh model provider too), base
URL, access token (write-only), and user ID — there is **no edit form**; changing a connection means
delete + re-create. Each panel gets a **Test connection** button that classifies failures readably:
unreachable network, invalid token, or user-ID mismatch. The delete dialog warns about capability o

verrides being removed and about dsh's default model pointing at the panel.
- **API keys** (per pane
l) — create, edit (name / group / quota / expiry / enable-disable), delete, and switch with one clic
k on *Use*. Editing happens **in place** like the official Models page: the row expands into an edit
or card (one card at a time), *Apply* writes immediately and keeps the card open on failure, and del
etions confirm in a dialog. Key material never crosses to the browser — creation responses are strip
ped server-side, and *create and set active* runs the regular switch flow so the secret only enters

the credential store.
- **Models** (per panel) — the models the active key can call with pricing, co
vering all three billing dialects of the panel family: per-token USD prices ($/1M tokens), fixed per
-call prices, and classic ratio pricing (model ratio × group ratio). Refreshing the list syncs it in

to dsh so running sessions pick it up immediately.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
- The plugin's state is its composition entry's config (a `panels` dict with each panel's connection
fields — the access token is a secret field redacted on the wire — plus the global knowledge base a
nd per-panel override groups; all fields are hot-editable `.volatile()` fields of the profile patch)
, it serves `/api/relay/{state,panels,panels-create,panels-delete,account,connection-test,keys,keys-
create,keys-update,keys-delete,use,models,capabilities,model-info,knowledge-refresh,dashboard,logs,l

ogs-stat,logs-meta}` inside dsh's authenticated web fence.
- On first key switch per panel it writes
the panel's pi-ai route profile (`api: openai-completions`, `baseURL: <panel>/v1`, `apiKeyEnv: RELA
Y_API_KEY_<PANEL>`, merged model catalog) into the `llm-pi-ai` entry's config — dsh hot-reloads rout

es, so no restart. The API key itself resolves per request from the panel's credential reference.
[该

no restart. The API key itself resolves per request from the panel's credential reference.
[该节后续省略]
## Security notes
- Each panel's access token lives in a secret settings field (redacted on every wire surface, includ
ing nested inside the panels dict); API keys are written only to the server-side credential store (`
.credentials.yaml`, 0600) and never returned to the browser — key creation responses are stripped se

rver-side, and no "copy key" feature exists.
- All plugin routes sit inside dsh's browser trust fenc

e (same origin + signed session); unauthenticated requests get 401.
- The models.dev lookup runs hos
t-side (cached, single-flight); the browser never talks to third parties directly. The preset fetch
never touches the relay panel and never introduces credentials.
## Compatibility
- Requires dsh ≥ **0.2.1-alpha.2** (`engines.dsh` enforces it) — the first host line with the entry-
config settings model this plugin's page and volatile hot writes build on. The host's frozen browser
module table supplies `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` (consumed as a stable-subset API; ins
talled as a devDependency **pinned to the host-matching version** for types only) and the storage st
ack (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage` as a peer dependency — dsh-base mounts the hub and the json backend
for every base-backed profile; on a profile without the stack the plugin degrades to a memory-only p

reset cache).
- The plugin deliberately sticks to the verified primitives subset (Button / Switch /
Pill / Tag / StateDot / Menu / Modal) and re-runs a browser walkthrough whenever the dsh dev depende
ncy is upgraded (see docs/PUBLISHING.md).
## Known limitations
- Management-API calls need the paired user ID (typed once per panel; see the panel's personal page)

.
- Model capacity falls back to id-prefix heuristics when neither the panel nor the knowledge base

reports a value; unknown ids fall back to 131072 context / 8192 output.
- Knowledge-base matching de
mands equality at every layer (case-fold, suffix strip, version-separator swap, variant completion)
and gives up on ambiguity; channel-named panel-specific models (e.g. `grok-video`) match nothing by

design.
- The preset only carries mainstream models — first-party providers released within the last
year. Panels selling older or niche models fall back to unconfigured; add your own entries or hit *

Refresh presets* (same rules).
- **First use needs one online fetch**: a fresh install (or a deleted
storage file) shows no preset entries until the first models.dev fetch succeeds; the knowledge base
, overrides, connections, and model sync all work regardless. Offline new installs stay in that stat

e until the host can reach models.dev (respecting the host's proxy environment).
- Upgrading from ≤0
.7.0: a stale `capabilityPresetDelta` key may linger in the profile patch. The new schema never decl
ares it, so the host treats it as an inert leftover — no errors, not projected, not writable. Ignore

it, or edit the profile patch by hand to drop the key.
- A panel's name is immutable after creation
(it keys the provider route, credential reference, and override group); renaming means delete + re-

add.
- Panels keep only recent usage-log detail and dashboard buckets; older data is the panel's ret

ention policy, not a plugin bug.
- models.dev is a third-party snapshot — unlisted models and toggle

-style reasoning fall back to manual configuration.
- Token-count shorthand is 1024-based (`128K` =
131072); a few vendors advertise decimal sizes (e.g. 200K = 200000), so check the live conversion hi
ndors advertise decimal sizes (e.g. 200K = 200000), so check the live conversion hint before saving.
